title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten distinct, documented spaces for individual work, computer-based research, group meetings, and academic support at Marist University.

cards.title: James A. Cannavino Library
cards.subtitle: Three-story library overlooking the campus green and Hudson River
cards.notes: Start with the library’s varied seating areas, then use its physical collections or borrow a laptop for work anywhere in the building.
cards.short_summary: A flexible campus library setting for solo or group coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist says Cannavino Library has seating for individual and group studying, 80 desktops, and laptops that may be used anywhere in the building.
cards.source_title: James A. Cannavino Library | Marist University
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours page before visiting; campus resources and borrowing may require Marist credentials.

cards.title: E-scriptorium
cards.subtitle: Cannavino Library computer lab
cards.notes: Use one of the 46 listed workstations when your assignment needs campus software, then save files to your preferred storage before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A library computer lab for research and software-based coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist’s family handbook identifies the E-scriptorium as the library’s largest computer lab, with 46 workstations and software supporting Marist classes.
cards.access_notes: Located in Cannavino Library; consult current library hours and workstation availability on arrival.

cards.title: Frank A. Fusco Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Cannavino Library reading room
cards.notes: Bring a reading-heavy task and settle into this named library room, documented with study furnishings for individual or small-group work.
cards.short_summary: A named reading-room environment inside the library.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist Archives documents the Frank A. Fusco Reading Room as part of the library’s study space, with options including soft seating, carrels, and tables.
cards.source_title: Marist Magazine, Summer 2000 | Marist Archives and Special Collections
cards.access_notes: This is within Cannavino Library; verify current room availability and library access before planning a session.

cards.entity_name: Margaret W. Mair Executive Presentation Room
cards.title: Margaret W. Mair Executive Presentation Room
cards.subtitle: Cannavino Library presentation setting
cards.notes: Use this room only for a presentation-focused session: organize slides, rehearse transitions, and confirm any room-use process with the library first.
cards.short_summary: A technology-equipped setting for presentation preparation.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist Archives identifies the Margaret W. Mair Executive Presentation Room and documents its large-screen projection and presentation technology.
cards.source_title: Marist Magazine, Summer 2000 | Marist Archives and Special Collections
cards.access_notes: A presentation-oriented room in Cannavino Library; confirm current reservation or access requirements with the library.

cards.title: Library 314 Study Room
cards.subtitle: Cannavino Library, Room 314
cards.notes: For a scheduled work block, use the Marist App reservation process listed by the university and arrive with your group’s materials ready.
cards.short_summary: A specifically identified library study room with a documented reservation workflow.
cards.evidence_claim: A Marist reservation guide lists Library 314 Study Room among locations that use the Marist App mobile reservation system.
cards.source_title: Mobile Scheduling of Shared Spaces on Campus | Marist University
cards.access_notes: Use the Marist App reservation instructions on the source page; availability and eligibility are not guaranteed.

cards.title: Presentation Practice Room
cards.subtitle: Cannavino Library
cards.notes: Reserve this room when you need to rehearse and record a talk; build in time to test the screen and camera before your practice run.
cards.short_summary: A library room designed around recorded presentation rehearsal.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist’s library map links to a page for reserving and using a Presentation Practice Room with a built-in presentation screen and camera.
cards.access_notes: Reservation is indicated by the library; use the linked room-reservation information to confirm current access details.

cards.title: Commons Lounge
cards.subtitle: Ground floor, Murray Student Center
cards.notes: Use the lounge for a laptop session or reading break; its listed seating, microwave, and coffee maker support longer on-campus stretches.
cards.short_summary: A Student Center lounge with documented study use and extended evening hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist describes the Commons Lounge as a ground-floor Student Center space used for studying, with seating and student amenities.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Mon–Thu 8:30 a.m.–1:30 a.m.; Fri 8:30 a.m.–2 a.m.; Sat–Sun 10 a.m.–2 a.m. The page frames it as a commuter space.

cards.title: Commuter Student Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Murray Student Center commuter area
cards.notes: Plan a group meeting around a reservable room with tables and chairs, and bring a laptop if you expect to use the listed printer.
cards.short_summary: Reservable Student Center group-work rooms with basic tech resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist’s commuter-student page lists reservable study rooms with tables and chairs for group meetings, plus laptops and a networked printer.
cards.access_notes: The resource is presented for commuter students; ask the Commuter Student Coordinator about current reservation eligibility.

cards.title: Marian Hall Quiet Study Room
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Marian Hall residence hall
cards.notes: If you live in Marian Hall, use the documented second-floor quiet room for a nearby focused session and respect residence-hall access rules.
cards.short_summary: A residence-hall quiet room available within Marian Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist identifies one quiet study room on the second floor of Marian Hall and states that building entry is by Marist ID-card swipe access.
cards.access_notes: Resident-hall access requires a Marist ID card; this space is most practical for Marian Hall residents.

cards.title: Academic Learning Center
cards.subtitle: Library 331, Cannavino Library
cards.notes: Pair independent study with academic support by checking in during office hours for tutoring, proofreading, counseling, or study-skills guidance.
cards.short_summary: A Library 331 academic-support hub for structured study help.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist lists the Academic Learning Center in Library 331 and says it provides academic support through tutoring, proofreading, and academic counseling.
cards.access_notes: Listed office hours are Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; services may have separate appointment procedures.
